Choosing a look

The rich-content themes

Each style in its light and its dark mode: the same diagram, chart, one-page PDF and HTML page. Pick one with use_theme("corporate-dark") in a build script, or for a whole project with a rich-content.json holding {"theme": "corporate", "mode": "dark"}. Every theme passes WCAG AA contrast (accessible, AAA), and its chart colours stay apart for colour-blind readers.

Technical

Design notes, architecture and engineering documents: the System Design manual's look, Crimson Pro to read and Geist to label, tinted boxes with soft corners.

Text Crimson Pro · headings Geist · labels Geist · code Geist Mono

Corporate

Client deliverables, board and status reports: Public Sans throughout, deep navy with a teal accent, quieter colours for the kinds, near-square corners and thin flat lines.

Text Public Sans · headings Public Sans · labels Public Sans · code Geist Mono

Editorial

Essays, analyses and white papers: Crimson Pro for headings and text, Public Sans for labels and charts, warm near-black ink, a deep red accent, and charts with nothing but horizontal gridlines.

Text Crimson Pro · headings Crimson Pro · labels Public Sans · code Geist Mono

editorial-light

editorial-dark

Minimal

One-pagers, summaries and anything shown on a screen: Geist alone, black and greys with one orange accent, square corners, boxes drawn as outlines whose kind is told by their icon and a coloured bar.

Text Geist · headings Geist · labels Geist · code Geist Mono

minimal-light

minimal-dark

Accessible

Documents for everyone, low vision and dyslexia included: Atkinson Hyperlegible, made so letters cannot be mistaken for each other, text at AAA contrast (7:1), thicker lines, and nothing told by colour alone.

Text Atkinson Hyperlegible Next · headings Atkinson Hyperlegible Next · labels Atkinson Hyperlegible Next · code Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono

Academic

Research reports, papers and chart-heavy analyses: EB Garamond for text, a classic book face, Public Sans for labels, the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito hues darkened to read as text, outlined frames with tick marks and no gridlines.
